chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra, from Al-Halby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who gave an advance payment for a servant of known age and known color, then he is given below his stipulation or above it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is from the goodwill of yourself and from him, then there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a servant provided after an advance payment differs in age or color from the agreement?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of *salam* (advance payment) contracts for slaves, emphasizing that deviations in specified attributes like age and color are permissible if accepted by mutual consent (*tibi nafs*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that flexibility in contractual terms is valid when rooted in the voluntary satisfaction of both parties, rather than strict adherence to initial specifications. It highlights the importance of *rida* (contentment) in commercial transactions within the Imami tradition.
